headlines.title: Flights halted at three US airports as watchdog warns over hacking threat
headlines.description: Senator Ron Wyden calls for swift action after GAO report finds systems guiding US aircraft vulnerable to interference A congressional watchdog has warned the systems guiding US aircraft are open to interference and deception as flights into three busy airports in the country’s north east US were halted by a radio equipment problem. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a ground stop at about 10am on Monday for Newark Liberty international, Philadelphia international and Teterboro airports, saying some radio frequencies at the Philadelphia terminal radar approach control (Tracon) were affected until the early afternoon. Arrivals and departures at Newark were delayed, and the agency has not said what caused the outage.

headlines.title: JD Vance says Trump’s White House media ban is ‘totally appropriate’ as networks halt TV pool coverage in response – live
headlines.description: NBC, ABC, CBS and Fox News, the fourth other networks that make up the White House TV pool, decided they would cease coverage in solidarity with banned CNN In the new complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on Monday, CNN, MS Now and Politico alleged that Trump had violated the First Amendment and due process by stripping the outlets of their White House access in a blatant act of retaliation for coverage he disliked.

headlines.title: First UK charges brought over 1994 Rwanda genocide
headlines.description: Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday charged with seven offences.

headlines.title: Rwandan man charged with crimes linked to 1994 genocide in first case brought in UK
headlines.description: Dr Vincent Brown will appear at Westminster magistrates court charged with seven offences A man has been charged with crimes linked to the genocide in Rwanda in 1994 in the first case of its kind to be brought in the UK. Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, who used to live in Kigali, the capital of Rwanda but now lives in Islington, north London, will appear at Westminster magistrates court on Tuesday charged with seven offences.

headlines.title: Aviation regulators turn to AI to help manage the nation's airspace
headlines.description: The Federal Aviation Administration launched an ambitious $875-million-dollar push to make the U.S. airspace more efficient. But critics say it won't solve bigger problems with air traffic control.

headlines.title: Charges dropped against Stanford students over pro-Palestine protest
headlines.description: Students faced prison terms and thousands of dollars in restitution over campus protest against Israel’s war on Gaza Five Stanford University students who faced prison sentences and thousands of dollars in restitution in connection to a campus protest against Israel’s war on Gaza had all charges dropped on Monday. The students also had their restitution severely reduced, ending a two-year legal saga that also saw the lead prosecutor in the case removed by the court.

headlinePool.title: Colombia declares public calamity as wildfire threatens popular tourist area
headlinePool.description: Wildfire forces evacuations and burns through mountains surrounding Villa de Leyva in the north-east Colombian authorities declared a public calamity as a wildfire burned through mountains surrounding one of the country’s best-known colonial towns in the north-east, scorching large swaths of vegetation and forcing evacuations. Nearly 20 active fires are burning across the South American country. Dry conditions have increased fire danger in Colombia as it braces for the effects of El Niño, which can help wildfires spread.

headlinePool.title: Two charged with woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds
headlinePool.description: The body of Jabulile Ntimba was the ninth to be found recently in an area east of Johannesburg.

headlinePool.title: Lauren Boebert says claims of sexual relationships with staffers ‘utterly false’
headlinePool.description: Republican congresswoman rejects ethics complaint and says allegations part of ‘politically motivated’ hit campaign Lauren Boebert, the firebrand Republican subject of a House ethics complaint that she had sex with three staff members, and paid one to keep quiet, has said the allegations are untrue – and part of a “politically motivated” campaign against her. Boebert’s denials came through a formal statement from her office, which said “the congresswoman rejects the claims as utterly false”. She also published a verbose video rant on social media in which she accused the person who filed the document as a “sloppy, desperate, obsessive hack” – and journalists who reported the story as falling victim to a “scam”.

headlinePool.title: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
headlinePool.description: The groups have been active in Ethiopia's most populous regions for years and now say they will work together.

headlinePool.title: No avoiding the cost of inaction on climate, Anthony Albanese says in New York
headlinePool.description: Before United Nations meeting, prime minister says Australians knows the impact of global heating as well as anyone Australia understands the dangers of global warming and the urgency of climate action as much as any other country, Anthony Albanese has said in a keynote speech shortly before the United Nations general assembly. Speaking at the opening of the Climate Week event at the UN in New York on Monday, the prime minister said Australians had experienced the impact of climate breakdown up close with a series of disastrous bushfires and floods in the past decades.

headlinePool.title: Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May 2026
headlinePool.description: A third-party cybersecurity firm accidentally gave experimental Gemini models access to the Internet.

headlinePool.title: Merz vows to keep coalition together for Germany's 'democratic future'
headlinePool.description: The chancellor has come under increasing pressure after resounding state election defeats, but says the results "go far beyond my own person"

headlinePool.title: Helen Jenner unveiled as Reform UK’s new leader in Wales after arrest of Dan Thomas
headlinePool.description: Nigel Farage dismisses loss of previous leader as ‘bump in the road’ and says party will ‘carry on as if nothing has happened’ Nigel Farage dismissed the loss of Reform UK’s leader in Wales last week as a “bump in the road” as the party unveiled a replacement. Helen Jenner replaces Dan Thomas, who stood down last Tuesday after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviours.

headlinePool.title: Wildlife will be affected by current drought for years to come, UK government says
headlinePool.description: The number of potentially damaging environmental incidents triggered by this year’s hot and dry weather has surpassed that of 2025 Wildlife in England and Wales will be affected by the current drought for years to come, the government has said. This summer saw large parts of England and all of Wales plunged into a serious drought, with both recording their driest Julys since records began in 1836.
